entities.name: Ivan III of Moscow
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Ivan III Vasilyevich, also known as Ivan the Great, was Grand Prince of Moscow and all Russia from 1462 until his death in 1505. Ivan served as the co-ruler and regent for his blind father Vasily II before he officially ascended the throne.

He consolidated Moscow's power, establishing it as the dominant force in Eastern Europe, and played a crucial role in the unification of the Russian principalities. Ivan's military campaigns and strategic alliances expanded Russia's borders, and he also promoted the development of Russian culture, architecture, and education.

Ivan's legacy continued to shape Russian history, with his son Vasily III succeeding him and further expanding Russian territory. The Ivan the Great statue in Moscow's Red Square remains a symbol of his enduring impact on Russian identity and national pride.

'Russia, as a state, was born from the womb of Ivan the Great's ambition,' said Russian historian Nikolai Karamzin in 1818.
